title: Coherence Training
subtitle: A frequency-specific correlation target with interpretive limits
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating coherence training within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain coherence training without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in coherence training.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to coherence training.

sections.explainSimply: Coherence estimates consistency of phase relationships across time within a frequency band.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Scalp coherence is influenced by distance, reference, volume conduction, data length and artifact. Higher or lower is not inherently healthier.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Training coherence assumes the metric is stable, specific and functionally meaningful for the individual—assumptions not routinely established clinically.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand coherence training to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Do not label every deviation as under- or overconnected pathology.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using coherence training predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Do not label every deviation as under- or overconnected pathology. Evidence classification: emerging; insufficient disorder-specific evidence.
